  > 
  > Re-checked against `results/` at fa1ab34:
  > - The clip paragraph now has b* above one on gene_expression, census_income and alphafold and below one on six sets. The 0.031 bound holds for n ≥ 100 (max 0.0310). census_income's unclipped coverage is 0.79 to 0.92 at n ≤ 300.

  > - The finite-population wording is limited to real-data cells.
  > - The new B5 text and the Table 1 note match: the T2 reference ratios are 1.004, 1.009, 1.004 and 1.009 against the strongest valid baseline. Neither baseline is valid in 2 of the 4 T2 cells and 5 of the 13 reference cells, as the double daggers say.
  > - The Results ranges match: 0.994 to 1.008 against the strongest valid baseline, 0.971 to 1.007 against the package, and the small-n median of 1.019 with range 0.927 to 1.116.
  > 
  > One optional nit, not blocking. The abstract and intro say "label saving at most 1.2%". The maximum against the strongest valid baseline is 1.13% (gene_expression, 1 − 0.9944²), so "at most 1.2%" is true but loose. "About 1.1%" would be exact. The 1.2% in the Results paragraph on n ≥ 300 is correct, because it is a width excess (1.012).
  > 
  > I did not check the rendered figures or tables, which belong to figtab-repo.
- pull_request review_requested in `paper-repo`#9 ("Version 1: how much shorter can a prediction-powered interval be?") by `ht-admin`- `internal-review-repo` pushed 69e08931ed2e
- pull_request_review_rejected reviewed in `paper-repo`#9 ("Version 1: how much shorter can a prediction-powered interval be?") by `internal-review-repo`  > Request changes on head 7ef2dac (document built from 7ef2dac28951). The paper's claims check out against results/ (headline.csv, cells.csv: ratios, 51-cell counts, validity marks, Prop. 1 re-derived), and it reads as a paper on the whole. Two small `must` items remain; full record: internal-review-repo/reviews/v1-pr9-7ef2dac.md.
  > 
  > **must**
  > 1. Abstract says the label saving is "at most 1.1%", the Introduction ("What we find") says "at most 1.2%". headline.csv gives 1 - 0.9943^2 = 1.13%. Make them agree, from the unrounded ratio.
  > 2. "A6", "B5" (Table 1 headers, Fig. 1 axis labels), the P/U "base class" column of Table 1 and the Fig. 2 panel title "C1: excess over floor" are internal identifiers the main text never defines. Use the names the text uses, define P/U in the caption (or drop the column) and drop the "C1" title (the venue also asks for no titles inside graphics).
  > 
  > **may** (owner decides; not holding the version)
  > 3. Results are dense (8-15 numbers per paragraph; the abstract carries ~15 numbers) and "the strongest-valid-baseline reading was fixed after the first results" is repeated in Sec. 4, the introduction and Sec. 7: say it once.
  > 4. The validity rule "Wilson upper < 0.95" calls 94.36% coverage at 5000 reps invalid (alphafold n=500) and puts 57 of 113 cells of Fig. 3 in "all fail": add a sensitivity line (e.g. tolerance 0.94) showing the headline classification does not depend on it.
  > 5. One sentence saying the strata-means class covers Fisch et al.'s stratified PPI, which is named as the closest relative but not run as published.
